title: U.S. House · California's 21st Congressional District
area: Fresno, Madera, and Merced counties in the central San Joaquin Valley.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 elections under Proposition 50, a mid-decade redistricting measure voters approved in a November 2025 special election.
In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, Jim Costa won 42.2% of the vote (43,461 votes) and Kyle Kirkland won 26.3% (27,076 votes), advancing them both to the November general election.

candidates.name: Jim Costa
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2005, under various district numbers)

summary.text: Jim Costa is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for California's 21st District, a Fresno-area farmer and former state legislator who has served in the House since 2005.

background.text: Born in Fresno, California, in 1952; earned a B.A. in political science from California State University, Fresno, in 1974.
Worked as a farmer; served in the California State Assembly from 1978 to 1994 and the California State Senate from 1994 to 2002.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry Subcommittee) and the House Committee on Foreign Affairs in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Kyle Kirkland
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2 top-two primary with 26.3% of the vote

summary.text: Kyle Kirkland is a Fresno-based businessman, casino owner, and former chairman of Steinway Musical Instruments, running for Congress for a third time.

background.text: Born in Virginia; earned an A.B. magna cum laude from Harvard College in 1984 and an M.B.A. from Stanford University in 1988.

Co-founded an investment banking firm in 1993 and served as chairman of Steinway Musical Instruments from 1993 to 2011. Owns and operates Club One Casino in Fresno and serves as president of the California Gaming Association and board chair of the Fresno Chaffee Zoo.

priorities.text: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey, named the economy as central to his campaign, saying a 'healthy market economy with limited regulation is the key to reducing the high cost of living.'
Called for securing the border and returning to enforcement of immigration law, and for addressing property crime.

positions.summary: Supports securing the border and enforcing immigration law, saying the country should not tolerate 'free-for-all' border policies.
positions.quote: We need to secure our borders and return to the enforcement of immigration law.

positions.summary: Favors limited government regulation and describes himself as understanding how the economy works as a business owner, without calling for higher taxes on high earners.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in California, 2026

researchNotes: Neither candidate has completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; Kirkland's positions are drawn from his 2024 survey answers (for the adjoining 20th District race he ran in that year), which may not reflect any 2026 platform changes. Jim Costa's positions/priorities are limited to committee assignments from official House records. Federal key votes and FEC totals for the incumbent are added separately by script.
